questions.q: What is the shared, org-wide daily limit on asynchronous Apex method executions?
options: 250,000 per 24-hour period, or the number of user licenses in the org multiplied by 200, whichever is greater
A flat 1,000 per day regardless of org size
Unlimited — there is no daily cap on asynchronous Apex executions
questions.explain: The daily asynchronous Apex execution limit is 250,000 or the org's user licenses multiplied by 200, whichever is greater — and it's a single shared pool across future methods, Queueable jobs, Batch Apex, and Scheduled Apex combined.

questions.q: Is this daily asynchronous execution limit a separate pool for each of the four async tools, or one shared pool?
options: One shared pool across future methods, Queueable jobs, Batch Apex, and Scheduled Apex combined
Each tool gets its own separate 250,000 daily limit
Only Batch Apex counts against any daily limit; the other three tools are unlimited
The limit only applies to Scheduled Apex jobs
questions.explain: All four asynchronous Apex tools draw from the same shared daily pool — a runaway process using one tool can reduce the capacity available to every other asynchronous job in the org for the rest of the day.

questions.q: Which per-transaction limits are higher in an asynchronous context than in a synchronous one?
options: SOQL queries issued (200 vs. 100) and heap size (12 MB vs. 6 MB)
DML statements (300 vs. 150) and callouts (200 vs. 100)
Total records retrieved by SOQL (100,000 vs. 50,000)
None — every per-transaction limit is identical between synchronous and asynchronous Apex
questions.explain: SOQL queries issued and heap size are both doubled in an asynchronous transaction (200 queries, 12 MB heap) compared to synchronous (100 queries, 6 MB heap). DML statements, total records retrieved by SOQL, and callouts stay the same between the two contexts.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of Scheduled Apex jobs that can be active in an org at any one time?
options: There is no cap on concurrently scheduled jobs
questions.explain: An org can have a maximum of 100 Scheduled Apex jobs active at any one time — a standing concurrency cap, independent of the shared daily execution-count limit.

questions.q: What does Limits.getQueueableJobs() let a developer do?
options: Check how many Queueable jobs the current transaction has already enqueued, to defensively avoid exceeding the per-transaction cap
Permanently increase the org's Queueable job limit
Cancel every currently running Queueable job
Return the total number of Batch Apex jobs that have ever run in the org
questions.explain: Limits.getQueueableJobs() reports how many Queueable jobs the current transaction has already enqueued, letting code check its own usage against the per-transaction cap before enqueuing more.
